clinical_knowledge.topic: Acute Cholecystitis in Pregnancy evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Acute Cholecystitis in Pregnancy is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes performing an RUQ ultrasound, starting IV fluids and pregnancy-safe antibiotics, and consulting OB/GYN and surgery, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: severe right upper quadrant pain, fever, and vomiting in a pregnant patient

Key HPI features: A 28-year-old female presents to the clinic with severe right upper quadrant pain, fever, and vomiting; she is currently pregnant. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Acute Cholecystitis in Pregnancy.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Acute Cholecystitis in Pregnancy.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Biliary colic without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Fever with right-upper-quadrant pain in pregnancy — needs urgent assessment given risk to both mother and baby.
management_principles: Perform RUQ ultrasound, start IV fluids, safe antibiotics, consult OB/GYN and surgery
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

teaching.one_liner: Pregnancy hormones make bile thicker and gallstones more likely; when a stone blocks the gallbladder, it becomes inflamed, causing right-upper-quadrant pain, fever, and vomiting.
